title: GPU preemption / scheduling stalls: detection, fast-reconcile workaround, and customer-facing guidance
author: Maya Chen
content:
H1: Summary

This page documents a recurring class of incidents observed in Dedicated deployments where GPU preemption or scheduling congestion produces multi-minute 'stalls' (request backpressure and token-generation latency spikes). It provides: a detection recipe, a recommended fast-reconcile workaround to restore tenant throughput quickly, customer-facing guidance for status updates, and long-term mitigation options.

H2: Impact

- Affected surface: Dedicated GPU tenants and burst workers; can also affect Private (on-prem) clusters with shared GPU pools.
- Symptom: streaming responses stall for 30s–300s, in-flight KV-cache misses, increased queueing latency, and elevated 5xx rates for generation endpoints.
- Business impact: degradation of latency SLOs (p95 token latency), customer-visible timeouts, and elevated support tickets during busy schedule windows.

H2: Root cause (common patterns)

1. Node-level preemption / pod eviction events when lower-priority pods are force-evicted to accommodate higher-priority workloads (spot reclaim, autoscaler-driven bin-packing).
2. Kube-scheduler congestion when many large-GPU requests are pending simultaneously and bin-packing heuristics thrash.
3. GPU driver or MIG state mis-synchronization after frequent container restarts causing pods to hang in 'RuntimeCreate' or 'ContainerCreating' for extended periods.

H2: Detection (what to watch for)

- Alert signals (examples):
  - sudden rise in kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total for inference pods
  - large increase in kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{reason=~".*Preempted|Evicted.*"}
  - sustained abnormally-high generation token-latency p95 > x ms (see SLO thresholds)
  - GPU utilization dips while queue length for inference requests stays high

- Example PromQL queries:
  - Pod eviction spikes (5m):
    increase(kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Failed"}[5m]) by (node)
